q1_issues.issue: `(Member sk_note_1 benchmark)` predicates a restrictive noun modifier of the group symbol; on a plural the instruction set requires either a fusing classifier riding the group's kind slot or a modifier distributed over the members, never a bare property on the group.

the scale `maturity` is nowhere in the text — "10-year" states a magnitude and unit but names no dimension, so the scale is supplied from world knowledge, against "point at the words that put the atom there"; the measure also sits on a group symbol, where a plural measure reads as the aggregate.

the `Measure` magnitude slot must hold a native number (or a `ParticleFromNormal` distribution); `(Fraction 17 32)` is the partitive proportion-level constructor used outside its defined slot, and the unit `point` appears nowhere in the text.
`(Measure sk_gain_1 price ...)` predicates a price of the gain EVENT rather than recording a delta — 17/32 is the size of the change, not the event's price.

q2_gaps: prenominal measure modifiers ("10-year notes", "a three-hour delay") — the `Measure` form needs a scale, and no rule supplies one when the text names only a magnitude and unit
a bond-quote bare fraction as a measured delta ("gained 17/32") — a fractional magnitude on a change-of-value verb has no licensed encoding (same delta gap as tierD-000147)
a proper-noun modifier inside a common-noun compound ("Treasury notes") — the fused `treasury_note` leaves the proper noun with no symbol and no `Name` fact
notes: `(Measure sk_note_1 yield 4.015 percent)` correctly follows the measure-verb -> dimension-noun rule ("weighs" -> `weight`), and the `Past` wrapper matches the matrix tense; the group-vs-per-note reading of that rate is left unstated by the instruction set.
